messages:
nora: Heads-up: running into a weird auth-retry loop with redwoodctl in a localtest container on Alpine. Token gets created, then immediately a 401 and redwoodctl tries to refresh, fails, repeats.

sam: hmm. Is this the same image you used for CI? any special mounts?

nora: no CI image, just alpine:3.18 + apk-installed redwoodctl. Using a mounted ~/.redwood symlink to host for profile sharing. Env: REDWOODCTL_LOCALTEST=1, REDWOOD_CONFIG_OVERLAY=/workspace/overlay.json

kai: can you paste the minimal logs? especially the auth lines.

nora: pasted below (scrubbed):
```
INFO  redwoodctl: login started
DEBUG token_store: write /home/dev/.redwood/tokens/prod.json
ERROR auth: request 401 POST https://auth.redwood.com/token (invalid_grant)
INFO  redwoodctl: attempting token refresh
DEBUG token_store: read /home/dev/.redwood/tokens/prod.json -> OK
ERROR auth: refresh failed: invalid_grant
INFO  redwoodctl: retrying login cycle
```

lee: two quick guesses: (1) overlay.json might contain an expired refresh token or malformed profile entry, (2) symlinked dotfiles + alpine UID mapping causing file permission 0xdeadbeef -> redwoodctl can't persist new token so it falls back to retry.

sam: also check timezone / clock skew inside the container. OAuth refresh fails are common with >5s skew.

nora: Clock is fine. I cat'ed the overlay file: it has a `profiles` entry created by the host with a `refresh_token` field. Maybe localtest expects ephemeral tokens and the overlay is forcing the CLI to use that stale refresh token.

kai: yeah that sounds likely. localtest mode should prefer device-code flow or a fresh ephemeral token. If overlay prepopulates a refresh_token, redwoodctl will try to use it. Suggest removing refresh_token from overlay or mark profile as source: host to skip refresh.

lee: workaround: mv ~/.redwood/tokens ~/.redwood/tokens.bak && run `redwoodctl login --device` in the container. If that succeeds, keep a wrapper that strips refresh_token when starting localtest.

nora: confirmed `redwoodctl login --device` succeeded after nuking tokens. But it still silently writes the token, then next run sees overlay refresh_token again and does the loop.

sam: maybe add a check: if REDWOODCTL_LOCALTEST=1 then prefer `token_source: ephemeral` over overlay refresh_token. Filing a small DX bug.

devex-bot: created issue #2412: "redwoodctl: localtest should ignore overlay refresh_token / prefer ephemeral auth" (assigned to devex).

kai: for a short-term fix in your environment, add a docker-entrypoint step that strips refresh_token keys from the overlay file before starting redwoodctl. e.g. `jq 'del(.profiles[].refresh_token)' /workspace/overlay.json > /workspace/overlay.clean.json`

nora: thanks everyone — working patch: https://gist.github.com/nora/strip-overlay-localtest (quick script). Will follow up with a PR if we want the CLI to hard-ignore refresh_token when LOCALTEST=1.

sam: pls include a regression test for symlinked token stores + UID mapping; we've tripped over that on WSL before.

nora: noted. I'll add a tiny test harness and attach logs to #2412. :thumbsup:
